name: Team Truce
tagline: Untangle conflict between people on your team
about: Team Truce helps managers untangle conflict between people on their team: map what's really going on, talk to each side, run a mediation that ends in agreements, reset the team afterwards and know when it's an HR matter.
persona: You are a workplace mediator: multipartial rather than neutral, curious about the interests behind positions, and clear-eyed about when something is misconduct rather than conflict.

onboarding.title: Conflict without the drama
onboarding.subtitle: Your team context helps calibrate what's normal.

tools.title: Map the conflict
tools.subtitle: Positions, interests, fears

inputs.label: What's happening
inputs.placeholder: Ana and Ben stopped talking after the launch; Ben says Ana took credit; Ana says Ben missed deadlines; the team is picking sides

tools.prompt: Map this conflict: {story}. Table (Party | Position | Likely underlying interest | Fear | What they need to hear), text with your read of the type — task, process, relationship or values — and how far it has escalated, bullets of what the manager may have contributed, and a callout on whether anything described crosses into harassment, discrimination or bullying that must go to HR.

tools.title: Talk to one side
tools.subtitle: A one-on-one that doesn't take sides

inputs.label: What you know of their view
inputs.placeholder: feels Ben undermines her in front of the team

tools.prompt: Prep a one-on-one with {who} about the conflict, given: {their}. Steps for a 30-minute conversation, a quote with an opening that doesn't take sides, bullets of 6 questions that move from venting to interests, a kv (what to promise, what not to promise, what to say if they ask what the other person said), and a callout on when to stop and escalate.

tools.title: Run a mediation
tools.subtitle: Ground rules to agreements

inputs.label: The issues on the table
inputs.placeholder: credit for the launch; missed deadlines; tone in code reviews

tools.prompt: Plan a {minutes}-minute mediation between {parties} on: {issues}. Steps with timings (ground rules, each side uninterrupted, reframing, options, agreements), a quote with the ground rules to read aloud, a table (Issue | Possible agreement | How we'll know it's kept), and a callout on what to do if one party refuses or it turns hostile.

tools.title: Reset the team
tools.subtitle: Recover the room after a fight

inputs.label: Where the team is now
inputs.placeholder: people still whisper; two juniors are anxious; Ben is quieter

tools.prompt: Plan a team reset after conflict given: {aftermath}, for the profile's team size and mode. Steps for the next 2 weeks (what the manager says in the team meeting, 1:1s to hold, norms to reinstate), a quote with a team-meeting statement under 120 words that acknowledges without airing details, a checklist of signals the team has recovered, and a callout on the mistake of pretending it didn't happen.

tools.title: HR or handle it?
tools.subtitle: Conflict, or conduct?

inputs.label: What happened, factually
inputs.placeholder: Ben called Ana 'hysterical' in a meeting; second time; Ana asked me to keep it quiet

tools.prompt: Assess: {facts}. Text with a clear view on whether this is a conflict to mediate or a conduct matter for HR and why, bullets of what the manager must do in the next 24 hours regardless, a quote with what to say to the person who asked for it to be kept quiet, and a callout on record-keeping and the limits of confidentiality a manager can promise.

disclaimer: General management guidance, not legal or HR advice. Employment rules vary by jurisdiction; follow your organisation's policies and involve HR or legal counsel on ratings, pay, conduct and employment decisions.
